Subject: Aurelia: mid-stage MAP — proposed compression & bridging plan

Hi Dana,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is a refresh of the Mutual Action Plan (v3) that reflects the milestones we discussed — evaluation gating, SOC2 evidence handoff, and the commit window for Dedicated/Private capacity. I highlighted two timing options: a standard lead-time path (10–12 weeks for a Private/VPC GPU tranche) and a compressed bridge we can attempt if Aurelia is able to shift acceptance criteria and sign within the next 2–3 weeks.

High-level ask from our side: if you want us to attempt the compressed route, confirm by EOD Thu (2026-04-30) so we can lock a short-term dedicated tranche and prioritize procurement. If procurement needs a formal SOW or an updated MAP with signature lines, say the word and we’ll produce that tomorrow.

Notes on capacity sizing (summary):
- Recommended initial pool: 32 x A100-equivalent vRAM nodes (mix of quantized variants) to meet your 40 req/s p95 target at 2x redundancy.
- If you compress to a 6–8 week runway, we’ll propose a two-tranche approach: 16-node dedicated bridge for the first 8 weeks + follow-on Private pool for production.

Attachments: Aurelia_MAP_v3.pdf (application/pdf) — MAP draft; details and acceptance checkpoints.

CCing Ben and Karthik to weigh in on technical/ops feasibility and Marissa for acceptance/SOC2 gating.

Best,

Thanks Hannah — high level looks good. A couple of operational clarifications from capacity/sales side:

1) Lead times: Historically Private/VPC single-tranche lead time averages 8–12 weeks from signed commitment to steady-state (hardware allocation + network/hardening). If we need to compress to ~6 weeks, we must glom a short dedicated tranche (reserved capacity) up front.

2) Sizing tolerance: The 32-node recomm is conservative. If Aurelia is open to additional quantization and aggressive batching, we can hit the target with 24 nodes for the MVP, but that reduces headroom for spikes. Recommend we size for 2x expected QPS headroom for the first 90 days.

3) Contingency options: short-term burst (hosted spare capacity) + dedicated bridge + accelerate private procurement. We'll need procurement timelines from Aurelia to validate.

I attached a quick sketch (in the MAP PDF) and will follow up with a formal GPU estimate workbook for the compressed scenario.

-ben

Dana — thanks for the clarity and for looping procurement. Short answer: the compressed 6-week runway is feasible with a bridging approach, subject to two constraints:

1) Commitment window: signed order + minimal SOW acceptance by 2026-05-11 so we can secure the dedicated tranche allocation for week-of-2026-05-25 provisioning.

2) Acceptance gating: we need a 48–72 hour staged acceptance window (smoke tests, perf run at p95 targets, and SOC2 evidence review). Marissa will manage the SOC2 handoff and acceptance checklist items.

What we propose (concrete):
- Week 0 (procurement sign): Reserve 16-node dedicated bridge (expedited allocation).
- Week 2–3: Provision bridge, run onboarding tests, ingest sample traffic.
- Week 4–6: Run canary at 50% traffic, validation runs.
- Week 6+: Cutover to Private/VPC pool (32 nodes target) or continue with two-phase scale depending on traffic.

I attached the GPU sizing workbook with the compressed scenario and the cost step-up for the expedited tranche. Bottom line: incremental 20–28% premium for the dedicated bridge compared to standard lead-time pricing.

Please see attachments: gpu_pool_estimate_Q2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

If that timeline works, Hannah — can you confirm we'll draft the SOW/MAP with signature lines and Ben — can you surface the expedited pricing? Marissa — please flag any SOC2 gaps that would block an accelerated acceptance.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
